# sngl://platforms is macro-only: it has no lib/platforms directory, only the
# per-target packages under it. It resolves against the macro registry, and
# unlike sngl://internal/marks it is public, so an ordinary program — or an
# out-of-tree platform plugin — may import it.
sngl check ok.sngl
stdout 'ok'

! sngl check internal.sngl
stderr 'internal to the compiler'

! sngl check nosuch.sngl
stderr 'unknown stdlib package'

-- ok.sngl --
import . "sngl://std"
import . "sngl://platforms"

#[options]
struct Knobs {
    gadget string = ""
}

component main {
    text(value="hello")
}

-- internal.sngl --
import . "sngl://std"
import . "sngl://internal/marks"

component main {
    text(value="hello")
}

-- nosuch.sngl --
import . "sngl://std"
import . "sngl://nosuch"

component main {
    text(value="hello")
}
